n = int(input())

# Constants
MAXN = 10**5 + 10
MOD = 10**9 + 7

# Helper function for modular exponentiation
def qpow(a, b):
    result = 1
    while b > 0:
        if b & 1:
            result = (result * a) % MOD
        a = (a * a) % MOD
        b >>= 1
    return result

# Initialize data structures
ch = [[0] * 64 for _ in range(MAXN)]
p = [[0] * 10 for _ in range(10)]
q = [[0] * 64 for _ in range(10)]
f = [[0] * MAXN for _ in range(10)]
id_map = {}
tt = 0

def dfs(s):
    nonlocal tt
    if s in id_map:
        return id_map[s]
    tt += 1
    id_map[s] = tt
    for i in range(1 << n):
        t = s
        for j in range(1 << n):
            for k in range(n):
                if (j >> k) & 1 and (i >> k) & 1 and ((s >> (j ^ (1 << k))) & 1):
                    t |= 1 << j
        ch[id_map[s]][i] = dfs(t)
    return id_map[s]

# Read input matrix p and normalize
dfs(1)
for i in range(n):
    row = list(map(int, input().split()))
    for j in range(n):
        p[i][j] = row[j]
        p[i][j] = (p[i][j] * qpow(100, MOD - 2)) % MOD

# Precompute q
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(1 << n):
        q[i][j] = 1
        for k in range(n):
            if (j >> k) & 1:
                q[i][j] = (q[i][j] * p[k][i]) % MOD
            else:
                q[i][j] = (q[i][j] * (MOD + 1 - p[k][i])) % MOD

# Initialize f
f[0][1] = 1

# Dynamic programming over n
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(1, tt + 1):
        for k in range(1 << n):
            ch_idx = ch[j][k]
            f[i + 1][ch_idx] = (f[i + 1][ch_idx] + f[i][j] * q[i][k]) % MOD

# Output result
if n < 6:
    print(f[n][id_map[(1 << (1 << n)) - 1]])
else:
    print(f[n][id_map[18446744073709551615]])
